method: self-consistency: minimise top-down occupied cells over 7 params
notes: tvec y = -0.25 m is CORRECT and physical, though it looks inverted at first.
The phone is mounted SIDEWAYS on the rig (rotated 90 deg right), and ARKit's
camera frame is device-fixed. Measured directly from the pose stream: world-up
expressed in the camera frame is -Y, with |cos| = 0.988 (walk 1) and 0.996
(walk 2). So camera -Y points up, and -0.25 m along Y means the lidar sits
25 cm ABOVE the camera — exactly the CAD geometry.
Do not 'fix' the sign. An earlier note blamed the portrait-locked UI; that was
wrong. ARKit's camera transform is independent of UI orientation and follows
Wall thickness of 4.2 cm still exceeds the 2 cm gate. The residual is drift,
not calibration: parameters cross-validate to 1.3 cm across two walks, while
thickness grows with window length (4.6 cm at 5 s, 7.4 cm at 40 s) and differs
between walks (4.23 vs 9.75 cm) on near-identical parameters. Phase 4's pose
graph and loop closure are what remove it.

frame_convention.meaning: camera -Y is up; phone mounted sideways (90 deg right)
